papers.title: Learning Linear Dynamical Systems with Semi-Parametric Least Squares
papers.abstract: We analyze a simple prefiltered variation of the least squares estimator for the problem of estimation with biased, semi-parametric noise, an error model studied more broadly in causal statistics and active learning. We prove an oracle inequality which demonstrates that this procedure provably mitigates the variance introduced by long-term dependencies. We then demonstrate that prefiltered least squares yields, to our knowledge, the first algorithm that provably estimates the parameters of partially-observed linear systems that attains rates which do not not incur a worst-case dependence on the rate at which these dependencies decay. The algorithm is provably consistent even for systems which satisfy the weaker marginal stability condition obeyed by many classical models based on Newtonian mechanics. In this context, our semi-parametric framework yields guarantees for both stochastic and worst-case noise.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究线性动力系统的参数估计，与FEA替代建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on system identification for linear dynamical systems with semi-parametric noise, with no application to finite element analysis, surrogate modeling, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决线性动力系统在偏置半参数噪声下的参数估计问题
summary_zh.method: 提出预滤波最小二乘估计器并证明其oracle不等式
summary_zh.result: 首次实现不依赖最坏情况衰减率的参数估计速率

summary_en.motivation: To address parameter estimation in linear dynamical systems under biased semi-parametric noise, which is common in causal statistics and active learning.
summary_en.method: A prefiltered least squares estimator is analyzed, and an oracle inequality is proven to mitigate variance from long-term dependencies.
summary_en.result: The proposed algorithm achieves provably consistent estimation rates without worst-case dependence on dependency decay, even under marginal stability.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical proofs only, no experimental or numerical validation.

papers.title: Particle Flow Bayes' Rule
papers.abstract: We present a particle flow realization of Bayes' rule, where an ODE-based neural operator is used to transport particles from a prior to its posterior after a new observation. We prove that such an ODE operator exists. Its neural parameterization can be trained in a meta-learning framework, allowing this operator to reason about the effect of an individual observation on the posterior, and thus generalize across different priors, observations and to sequential Bayesian inference. We demonstrated the generalization ability of our particle flow Bayes operator in several canonical and high dimensional examples.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA surrogate modeling, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification for biomechanical design, or implant-specific applications.

summary_en.motivation: To realize Bayes' rule via a particle flow approach using neural ODEs for efficient posterior inference.
summary_en.method: An ODE-based neural operator is trained in a meta-learning framework to transport particles from prior to posterior given observations.
summary_en.result: The method generalizes across different priors, observations, and sequential inference tasks in canonical and high-dimensional examples.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on numerical benchmarks including canonical and high-dimensional problems.
